response.title: Can a power station run an electric pressure washer and a shop vacuum for mobile car detailing instead of a generator?
response.answer:
Yes. A portable power station can run an electric pressure washer and a shop vacuum for mobile car detailing without a gas generator. In fact, a properly sized power station can be a great option for a mobile detailing business because it's quieter, produces no exhaust, and requires less maintenance.

However, there's one important catch: You need enough inverter power to start the motors and enough battery capacity to finish multiple cars.

1. How much power do you need?

Typical power requirements for mobile detailing equipment:

Equipment

Startup surge (approx.)




Small electric pressure washer

	

1,200–1,600W

Compact shop vacuum

1,200–2,400W




Large shop vacuum

	

1,200–1,500W

	

2,000–3,000W




DA polisher

	

400–900W

	

Varies

Actual startup requirements depend on the motor and model.

For example, if your pressure washer draws 1,500W and your vacuum draws 1,000W:

Running separately: You need an inverter that supports at least 1,500W, plus sufficient startup surge capability.

Running simultaneously: You need at least 2,500W of continuous output, ideally with some headroom.

My suggested target for a mobile detailing business is a 3,000W pure sine wave power station with a 2–4kWh battery. That gives you flexibility for pressure washing, vacuuming, and polishing, although exact compatibility still depends on motor startup demands.

2. How many cars can you detail on one charge?

Let's assume:

Pressure washer: 1,500W, operating 15 minutes per car

Shop vacuum: 1,000W, operating 20 minutes per car

Other tools: 100Wh per car

That works out to approximately 810Wh per car, including an allowance for inverter losses.

markup:
**Yes. A portable power station can run an electric pressure washer and a shop vacuum for mobile car detailing without a gas generator.** In fact, a properly sized power station can be a great option for a mobile detailing business because it's quieter, produces no exhaust, and requires less maintenance.

However, there's one important catch: **You need enough inverter power to start the motors and enough battery capacity to finish multiple cars.**

## 1. How much power do you need?

Typical power requirements for mobile detailing equipment:

| Equipment | Running power | Startup surge (approx.) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Small electric pressure washer | 1,200–1,600W | 1,800–3,000W |
| Compact shop vacuum | 700–1,200W | 1,200–2,400W |
| Large shop vacuum | 1,200–1,500W | 2,000–3,000W |
| DA polisher | 400–900W | Varies |

Actual startup requirements depend on the motor and model.

For example, if your pressure washer draws 1,500W and your vacuum draws 1,000W:

- Running separately: You need an inverter that supports at least 1,500W, plus sufficient startup surge capability.
- Running simultaneously: You need at least 2,500W of continuous output, ideally with some headroom.

**My suggested target for a mobile detailing business is a 3,000W pure sine wave power station with a 2–4kWh battery.** That gives you flexibility for pressure washing, vacuuming, and polishing, although exact compatibility still depends on motor startup demands.

## 2. How many cars can you detail on one charge?

Let's assume:

- Pressure washer: 1,500W, operating 15 minutes per car
- Shop vacuum: 1,000W, operating 20 minutes per car
- Other tools: 100Wh per car

That works out to approximately **810Wh per car**, including an allowance for inverter losses.

<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <text weight="medium">Estimated cars per charge</text>
  <text color="secondary" size="xs">Based on the example workload above, 85% usable battery energy, and no recharging between cars.</text>
  {@body const [battery,setBattery] = DIL.useState("2048")}
  <radio-group direction="col" value={battery} onChange={setBattery}>
    <radio value="1024">1kWh battery</radio>
    <radio value="2048">2kWh battery</radio>
    <radio value="4096">4kWh battery</radio>
    <radio value="6144">6kWh battery</radio>
  </radio-group>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align="end" justify="between">
    <box gap={1}>
      <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{Math.floor(Number(battery)*0.85/810)} cars</title>
      <caption>Estimated complete jobs</caption>
    </box>
    <box gap={1} align="end">
      <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{Math.round(Number(battery)*0.85/810*10)/10}</title>
      <caption>Jobs worth of energy</caption>
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

Real-world results depend heavily on how long you actually run the equipment.

## 3. Power station vs. gas generator

| | Power station | Gas generator |
|---|---|---|
| Noise | Very quiet | Noisy |
| Exhaust | None | Yes |
| Maintenance | Minimal | Regular |
| Runtime | Limited by battery | Refill with gas |
| Initial cost | Usually higher | Usually lower |
| Residential detailing | Excellent | Good, but noisier |

Battery power stations are particularly appealing for residential mobile detailing where customers appreciate quiet operation.

## 4. What I would choose

For a solo detailer doing 2–3 cars per day, I'd aim for:

- **3,000W continuous AC output**
- **At least 4,000–6,000W startup surge capability**, subject to equipment specifications
- **3–4kWh battery capacity**
- LiFePO4 battery chemistry
- Pure sine wave inverter
- Suitable weather protection and GFCI protection for wet work

A smaller 2kWh station may work if you're careful with your equipment usage. Motor startup is a real consideration, especially with pressure washers that restart every time you squeeze the trigger. <Cite refs={["turn505065search3","turn505065search6"]}/>

## 5. Two questions that will determine your ideal setup

{@body const [washer,setWasher] = DIL.useState("unknown")}
{@body const [vac,setVac] = DIL.useState("unknown")}
{@body const [cars,setCars] = DIL.useState("3")}
{@body const [together,setTogether] = DIL.useState("separate")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Help me size a battery power station for mobile detailing. Pressure washer: "+washer+". Shop vacuum: "+vac+". Cars per day: "+cars+". Equipment operation: "+together+". Recommend suitable inverter wattage, battery capacity, and specific power stations.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Pressure washer model or power rating</label>
      <input placeholder="e.g. Active 2.0, 120V 13A" value={washer==="unknown"?"":washer} onChange={setWasher}/>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Shop vacuum model or power rating</label>
      <input placeholder="e.g. RIDGID 4-gallon, 9A" value={vac==="unknown"?"":vac} onChange={setVac}/>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>How many cars per day?</label>
      <radio-group direction="row" value={cars} onChange={setCars}>
        <radio value="1">1</radio>
        <radio value="2">2</radio>
        <radio value="3">3</radio>
        <radio value="4+">4+</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Will you use both machines at the same time?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={together} onChange={setTogether}>
        <radio value="separate">No, one at a time</radio>
        <radio value="simultaneous">Yes, simultaneously</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Find the right power station <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

With those details, I can narrow down whether a 2kWh setup is sufficient or whether you need a larger system to replace a gas generator reliably.
